vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: privacy-policy
Version: 1.0.3

The Privacy Policy Generator is a straightforward utility for generating legal document templates (Standard, GDPR, and CCPA). The core logic in `scripts/privacy.sh` is a simple bash script that accepts user-defined arguments (company name, email, etc.) and outputs pre-defined text templates to stdout; it contains no network calls, file system writes, or data exfiltration risks.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it generates privacy-policy text locally using a bundled shell script, requests no credentials, has no install steps, and does not appear to perform network I/O or access unrelated system data.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (privacy policy generator, GDPR/CCPA, app/website) match the included assets: SKILL.md documents commands for generation and scripts/privacy.sh contains template generation logic. Nothing requested (no env vars, no binaries) is unexpected for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local commands (generate, gdpr, ccpa, etc.). The bundled script prints policy templates based on provided arguments and placeholders. There are no instructions to read unrelated files, harvest system state, or exfiltrate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only with a local script). The script is bundled with the skill; nothing is downloaded or extracted from external URLs.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. The script uses only date and command-line arguments (company, email, website, etc.), which is proportionate to generating policy text.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward local template generator. Before installing, consider: (1) inspect the full scripts/privacy.sh file yourself (to check for any hidden network calls or command execution not shown), (2) run the script in a sandbox or non-production environment to verify behavior, and (3) remember the SPDX/legal disclaimer in the tool: generated policies are for reference only—consult a lawyer for legal compliance. If you need absolute assurance, request the skill source origin or an integrity signature from the publisher.
